name: Mitochondrial Disease with Dilated Cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Mitochondrial Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Presence of dilated cardiomyopathy confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Evidence of mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme deficiency in muscle biopsy or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA or nuclear DNA mutations associated with mitochondrial disease
Presence of neurological symptoms consistent with mitochondrial disease (e.g., muscle weakness, seizures)
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of dilated cardiomyopathy plus biochemical evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction and/or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction
searchTerms: enlarged heart with poor pumping function
dilated cardiomyopathy with low ejection fraction
heart muscle disease causing weak contractions

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via muscle biopsy or fibroblast analysis
searchTerms: deficiency in cell energy production enzymes
weakness in upper arm and thigh muscles
chronic low energy related to mitochondria
drooping eyelids or eye muscle weakness
weakness of eyelid and eye muscles
endocrine issues including high blood sugar

laboratory: Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity
imaging: Echocardiogram showing dilated left ventricle with reduced systolic function
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial fibrosis and dilation
Brain MRI may show stroke-like lesions or basal ganglia abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA (e.g., MT-TL1, MT-ND genes)
Nuclear gene mutations affecting mitochondrial function (e.g., POLG, TK2)
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology

distinguishingFeatures: No pathogenic mitochondrial DNA or nuclear mutations
Lack of multisystem involvement typical of mitochondrial disease
No evidence of dilated cardiomyopathy on imaging
Predominant neurological or muscular symptoms without cardiac involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms in young patient
Multisystem involvement including neurological and muscular symptoms
Family history of mitochondrial disease or unexplained cardiomyopathy
